sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Suresh Chandra Dwivedi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saumitra Dayal Singh,J.

Heard Sri Suresh Chandra Dwivedi learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Ankit Srivastava learned AGA for the State.
Challenge has been raised to the order dated 30.7.2022 passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kaushambi in Case Crime No. 90 of 2002 under Sections 420, 379, 411 IPC and under Rule 3/57 of the U.P. Mines Mineral (Concession)Rules, 1963 in respect of applicant No. 1 and to quash the charge sheet, cognizance order and the order dated 30.7.2022 in respect of applicant Nos. 2 to 4.
Submission is, in view of further order of the Supreme Court in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd and Another Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 440 dated 25.4.2022,
the original interim protection granted by this Court in Application U/S 482 No. 11407 of 2002,
Kapil Muni Karwaria Vs. State of U.P. and Others, dated 13.12.2002 continues to have force.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned AGA would submit, the only exception that may have been carved out by the Supreme Court in the order referred to by learned counsel for the applicant would be an order passed in exercise of extraordinary jurisdiction of the Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

Inasmuch as the interim order relied upon by learned counsel for the applicant was passed not under Article 226 of the Constitution but under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the benefit being claimed is not available to the applicants.

The fact that no stay vacation application has been filed in the pending application and no specific order may have been passed, may not be of any avail to the applicant in view of the law declared by the Supreme Court in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd and Another Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, (2018) 16 SCC 299.

entities.text: Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd and Another Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, (2018) 16 SCC 299
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsel for parties and having perused the record, harsh as it may appear, it cannot be disputed that the interim order passed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. may not survive beyond six months unless extended by reasons to be recorded by the Court.
Undisputedly, the order dated 13.12.2002 passed in Application U/S 482 No. 11407 of 2002 has not been extended till date.
In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd and Another Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, (2018) 16 SCC 299, no interim order exists.

entities.text: Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd and Another Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, (2018) 16 SCC 299
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The exception claimed on the strength of the subsequent order passed by the Supreme Court dated 25.4.2022, is not available to the applicant as the interim order dated 13.12.2002 being referred to was passed in exercise of statutory powers of the Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and not under the extraordinary constitutional jurisdiction of the Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
Accordingly, the instant application fails and is dismissed.
It is however left open to the applicants to seek appropriate relief in the pending Application U/S 482 No. 11407 of 2002.
